entries.value: "`bsc lan` one-way multicast wire contract: the datagram every emit-only sensor sends and every subscriber verifies. Pure codec — no sockets, no filesystem, no async runtime."

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# Confidentiality: a GROUP key, so one emission serves N subscribers.
# Authenticity: the sensor signs. A subscriber holding the group key can READ
# the stream but must never be able to FORGE into it -- with a shared key
# alone, every subscriber could fabricate alerts, and that gets worse with
# every device added. Reuses curve25519-dalek, which snow already pulls in.
# NO I/O. This crate is the contract, not the transport (the same split
# crates/bsc-tunnel draws between its protocol and its channel), which is what
# lets every property below be tested on a laptop with no sensor hardware.
# tests/no_io.rs pins it against this crate's own resolved dependency closure.
sections.name: [dependencies]

lead: # THE TEST SOURCE IS IN THE GRAPH, not in this directory
# (`a-rust-record-test-runs-and-an-edge-reaches-the-seed`). `tests/wire_contract.rs` does not exist:
# the whole file is the `bsc-lan-stream--wire-contract` EDGE in graph/algorithms.json, which also
# records the four member records it spans. The shared build script materializes it into
# `$OUT_DIR/tests/wire_contract.rs` and the shared root below `include!`s it, so `cargo nextest`
# compiles and runs it as an ordinary integration test — from OUTSIDE the crate, against the public
# API, which is exactly what a `tests/` target is for and what re-homing it as a `#[cfg(test)] mod`
# would have silently given up.
# To change it, edit the EDGE and promote it — editing a file here would be editing nothing:
#     bsc graph edge get bsc-lan-stream--wire-contract
#     bsc graph edge set --id bsc-lan-stream--wire-contract --members <...> --src <file>
#     bsc graph promote --id bsc-lan-stream--wire-contract --root "$PWD"
sections.name: [[test]]
